name: Medicine ball throw and slam
pattern: Throw a weighted ball as fast as you can: legs and hips start the push, the trunk passes it on, the arms release.
setup: Pick a ball light enough to move fast: about 2-6 kg for most throws.
Feet shoulder width, knees soft, ball held in both hands.
Clear space in front, or face a solid wall for rebounds.

steps.text: Rise onto your toes and reach the ball overhead, body long.
Fold at the hips and pull the ball down hard, throwing it at the floor just in front of your feet.
Squat with a flat back to pick it up after the bounce.
Stand and go straight into the next reach.

cues.cue: Throw with your hips, not just your arms.
cues.why: Throw distance tracks lower body power: leg drive and hip extension power the backward overhead throw.

cues.cue: Light ball, max speed every rep.
cues.why: Ball speed falls as mass rises; lighter balls train speed of release.

cues.cue: Brace your middle as you throw.
cues.why: The trunk passes force from the legs to the arms; a loose trunk leaks it.

cues.cue: Flat back when you pick it up.
cues.why: Many reps of rounded lifting add up on the lower back.
Overhead throws ask the shoulder to slow the arm after release; a full follow-through spreads the load.

breathing: Breathe in on the reach or load, breathe out sharply as you throw.

tempo.note: Explosive. Rest between reps for power; go continuous for conditioning.

mistakes.name: Arms only
mistakes.looks: The torso stays upright and only the arms swing the ball.
mistakes.fix: Hinge hard at the hips; the chest follows the ball down (or the hips turn first in a rotational throw).
mistakes.why: The big leg and hip muscles do not help, so the throw is weak.

mistakes.name: Rounded back pickup
mistakes.looks: Legs straight and back curled when picking the ball up.
mistakes.fix: Bend the knees and squat down to it.
mistakes.why: Repeated rounded lifts strain the lower back.

mistakes.name: Arching overhead
mistakes.looks: Ribs flare and the lower back bends back at the top.
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, reach tall without leaning back.
mistakes.why: It loads the lower back instead of stretching the trunk muscles.

safety: Slam only a dead-bounce slam ball; a rubber medicine ball can rebound into your face.
Stand side-on to a wall for rotational throws and leave room for the bounce.
Shoulder pain: use chest passes and scoop tosses instead of overhead throws.

variants.change: Push the ball from the chest like a jump into a push; on the back, throw straight up and catch.
Side-on, turn the back hip then the trunk, release past the front hip.
Scoop between the legs and throw back over your head with a jump: a full triple extension.
Ball behind the head, step and throw forward like a soccer throw-in.
Front squat to full depth, drive up and throw to a target about 3 m high, catch into the next squat. Conditioning: about 7.5 MET (vigorous calisthenics).
Sit-up into a throw or slam: a trunk flexion exercise.
One-hand slam: same hinge, add a trunk rotation.
Circle the ball around the head before the slam.

subtypes.name: Chest pass
subtypes.change: Ball at the chest, step or jump forward and push both arms straight.

subtypes.name: Rotational throw
subtypes.change: Side-on to the wall; load into the back hip, then hips, trunk and arms turn in order.

subtypes.name: Backward overhead toss
subtypes.change: Squat with the ball between the knees, then jump and swing it straight-armed back over the head.

subtypes.name: Wall ball
subtypes.change: Ball at the chest, full front squat, drive up and throw high to the wall, catch into the next squat.

motion.basis: Lower body and trunk contribution from stockbrugger2003 and hardy2025; ball mass effects from vandentillaar2013; overhead shoulder demands from cordasco1996. Joint angles are estimates, not measured values.
